new_jobs.description:
Position Description & Qualifications

Environmental Specialist Mid HI, TO647(35534)

This position is contingent upon contract award, customer approval, and the availability of funding. The final scope, responsibilities, work location, schedule, position requirements, and employment start date may change based on final contract requirements.

Are you looking for an Environmental Specialist role where you can directly shape installation compliance, conservation, and environmental risk management? Join Serco and Team KIRA in supporting the 647th Civil Engineer Squadron (647 CES) at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam (JBPHH).

As a Mid-Level Environmental Specialist, you will support the transition of environmental records, facility documentation, and compliance programs from Navy systems into Air Force authoritative repositories. Your work will help ensure environmental information is accurate, organized, and available to support compliance, Activity Management Plans (AMPs), project development, and installation decision-making.

You will manage environmental compliance and conservation activities, coordinate with regulators and mission partners, support hazardous material requirements, conduct inspections and field assessments, and provide environmental input for facility and infrastructure projects.

Why Join Serco and Team KIRA?

Support environmental stewardship and mission readiness across Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam.
Help establish a high-integrity baseline of environmental records, compliance documentation, and program data.
Provide defensible environmental recommendations that support installation planning and decision-making.
Collaborate with an integrated team supporting the transition of environmental, facility, utility, and real property programs from Navy oversight to Air Force stewardship.

As a Mid-Level Environmental Specialist, You Will

Manage day-to-day environmental compliance, conservation, stewardship, and sustainability activities in accordance with applicable federal, state, Department of Defense, and Air Force requirements.
Identify environmental compliance risks, required actions, mitigation measures, and abatement needs.
Prepare technical environmental program documentation and support compliance reviews.
Provide environmental planning input for facility, utility, and infrastructure projects to help integrate environmental requirements early in project development.
Lead the transfer, validation, organization, and upload of environmental documentation from Navy systems into Air Force repositories, including NexGen IT and SharePoint.
Ensure transferred records comply with Air Force records management standards and support environmental program audits, quality reviews, and installation decision-making.
Coordinate with regulators, host and tenant organizations, mission partners, and community groups.
Develop and review environmental permits, regulatory submittals, compliance actions, and response packages for notices of violation.
Conduct internal environmental inspections and maintain inspection criteria, schedules, and checklists.
Perform fieldwork involving water, soil, asbestos, lead-based paint, wildlife, and environmental hazard assessments.
Document inspection and assessment findings and track corrective actions through closure.
Complete or validate hazardous material survey reports and develop environmental condition assessments for abatement or remediation projects.
Conduct weekly environmental data collection and analysis.
Prepare technical reports, briefings, and visual media products for program stakeholders.
Support environmental documentation required for Advisory and Assistance Services (A&AS) deliverables, including Activity Management Plan inputs, DD Form 1391 environmental components, and project development packages.
Other duties may be assigned.

To Be Successful In This Role, You’ll Have

A bachelor’s degree from an accredited United States institution in environmental science, environmental engineering, biology, chemistry, or a related natural science field.
At least three years of experience supporting military facilities or infrastructure.
At least five years of environmental program management experience.
The ability to obtain and maintain a Tier 1 background investigation and Common Access Card (CAC) for access to Air Force systems.
The ability to comply with applicable Air Force environmental, safety, operations security, cybersecurity, Non-classified Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNet) user, and records management requirements.
The ability to conduct environmental inspections, assessments, sampling, and other required fieldwork.
Strong technical writing, data analysis, documentation, and stakeholder coordination skills.

Preferred Qualifications

A current U.S. Department of Defense Secret security clearance.
Experience developing environmental project plans, specifications, cost estimates, and mitigation strategies.
Experience conducting hazardous material surveys, supporting abatement oversight, and performing environmental data quality reviews.
Familiarity with GeoBase, Spatial Data Standards for Facilities, Infrastructure, and Environment (SDSFIE), or military installation mapping requirements.
Experience performing Geographic Information System (GIS) data validation, topology checks, attribute reviews, or metadata maintenance.
Experience with ACES, NexGen IT, TRIRIGA, BUILDER, PAVER, SharePoint, or similar systems.
Experience with data migration, public works, installation planning, or civil engineering datasets.
Experience preparing environmental inputs for Activity Management Plans, DD Form 1391 documentation, or military facility project development packages.

Location and Schedule

This proposed position is expected to be performed on-site at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, Hawaii. Current Hawaii residency is preferred. The anticipated schedule is Monday through Friday during normal business hours.

Additional Requirements

The selected candidate must obtain and maintain the required background investigation, credentials, and access to Air Force systems.
The selected candidate must comply with applicable environmental, safety, operations security, cybersecurity, network use, and records management policies.

We help our clients deliver vital services more efficiently while increasing the satisfaction of their end customers. TRC, Member of WSP, is a global consulting environmental and engineering firm and one of the top design firms in the energy sector. new_jobs.title: Data Coordinator, Transplant
new_jobs.description:
When you join the growing BILH team, you're not just taking a job, you’re making a difference in people’s lives.

Our Transplant Institute team is a multidisciplinary group of experts who are committed to compassionate patient involvement throughout the entire transplant process: the initial evaluation, pre-transplant care, transplant surgery and follow-up care.

The Data Coordinator supports the Transplant Department at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, MA. Following 3-6 months of training, this role may work primarily remotely.

Job Description

Maintains data capture, storage, and retrieval interfaces for the purposes of clinical care, outcome monitoring, quality improvement, and clinical research. Remote/ hybrid work option available.

Essential Responsibilities

Collects and enters clinical data from paper and electronic sources into a database(s).
Interacts with clinical staff to determine data collection needs; recommends key data fields, sources and process for data collection.
Integrates clinical data from multiple points of service.
Monitors data to ensure that it is formatted accurately and reflective of the care elements provided.
Performs routine audits of clinical data base to ensure data integrity and collaborates with department Systems Administrator and end users to correct issues.

Required Qualifications

High School diploma or GED required. Bachelor's degree preferred.
0-1 years related work experience required.
Experience in medical terminology.
Advanced skills with Microsoft applications which may include Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint or Access and other web-based applications. May produce complex documents, perform analysis and maintain databases.

Competencies

Decision Making: Ability to make decisions that are guided by general instructions and practices requiring some interpretation. May make recommendations for solving problems of moderate complexity and importance.
Problem Solving: Ability to address problems that are varied, requiring analysis or interpretation of the situation using direct observation, knowledge and skills based on general precedents.
Independence of Action: Ability to follow precedents and procedures. May set priorities and organize work within general guidelines. Seeks assistance when confronted with difficult and/or unpredictable situations. Work progress is monitored by supervisor/manager.
Written Communications: Ability to communicate clearly and effectively in written English with internal and external customers.
Oral Communications: Ability to comprehend and converse in English to communicate effectively with medical center staff, patients, families and external customers.

Fall (September – January): 8:30am – 4:30pm; 25-39 hours per week

Job Description:
The Adjunct Conservation Educator will support the implementation of two internship programs—Project TRUE (Teens Researching Urban Ecology) and the Emerging Leaders in Conservation Solutions Internship (ELCSI)—providing coordination, mentorship, instruction, and support to both high school and undergraduate/trade school students.
Project TRUE (Teens Researching Urban Ecology) May – September
Project TRUE is a 21-week research mentoring program for rising high school juniors and seniors from the Bronx, providing hands-on urban ecology research experiences and mentorship from undergraduate students and STEM professionals. The Adjunct Educator will assist with the implementation and coordination of the program, collaborating with the Project TRUE leadership team to support and co-mentor undergraduate and high school students as they develop and conduct authentic research projects at the Bronx Zoo. The Educator will support the planning and facilitation of science and mentorship curriculum, guide students through research project development, data collection and analysis, and help students synthesize and communicate their findings.
Emerging Leaders in Climate Solutions Internship (ELCSI) September – April
ELCSI is a new internship opportunity for undergraduate and trade school students who are not pursuing STEM fields but are interested in exploring how climate solutions can be incorporated into their future careers. The program provides foundational knowledge of climate science and climate change through hands-on learning and field experiences that introduce interns to a range of careers connected to climate solutions. As the primary point of contact for ELCS, the Adjunct Educator will lead the day-to-day implementation and coordination of the internship, serving as a facilitator, mentor, and instructor for a cohort of 15–20 interns. The Adjunct Educator will coordinate field experiences, develop and facilitate learning activities aligned with program objectives and outcomes, and provide guidance and support as interns develop their culminating projects and reports. Across both programs, the Adjunct Educator will foster meaningful learning experiences, provide mentorship, and help inspire the next generation of conservation and environmental professionals.

Responsibilities:
Adjunct Conservation Educator - Internships will…

Serve as an educator, mentor, and facilitator for high school, undergraduate, and trade school participants, sharing knowledge and enthusiasm for urban ecology, climate science, conservation, and scientific research.

Assist with the development, adaptation, and facilitation of science research and mentorship curriculum, including lessons and hands-on activities. (Project TRUE)

Guide students through authentic research projects, including experimental design, field methods, data collection and analysis, synthesis of findings, and development of research posters and abstracts. (Project TRUE)

Serve as the primary point of contact for the Conservation Solutions Internship, coordinating program activities, communication, logistics, and day-to-day implementation. (ELCS)

Coordinate fieldwork, field trips, and experiential learning opportunities that connect ELCS participants to climate science, conservation, and related career pathways. (ELCS)

Teach lessons and facilitate hands-on learning experiences in classroom, zoo, outdoor, and field research settings, and support ELCS participants in developing culminating projects and reports.

Collaborate with program staff, mentors, scientists, educators, and external partners to support effective program implementation and meaningful participant experiences (ELCS)

Prepare and maintain program materials, supplies, and research equipment; monitor participant engagement; and provide mentorship and guidance to support participants’ academic and professional development.

Perform other related duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Qualification Requirements

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in science, education, or related field

One-year prior teaching or mentorship experience

Ability to work within a highly team-oriented environment, as well as independently

Excellent verbal communication skills to help interpret science concepts and to coordinate with others

Reliable, flexible, and accountable

Willingness to travel to field locations throughout the 5 boroughs

Must be able to lift and carry up to 20lbs and face the rigors of fieldwork including long periods of time outdoors, large amounts of walking and standing, and exposure to the elements and rugged/overgrown terrain

Educational background in ecology, environmental science or education preferred

Valid driver’s license preferred

new_jobs.description:
Overview

If you’re ready for more than a job, Critter Control offers a career with purpose.

Are you looking for a hands-on career, not just a job? Do you have experience in construction, roofing, insulation, or home improvement and want to put those skills to work in a stable, recession-resistant industry?

Critter Control Operations specializes in wildlife management services for residential and commercial properties, providing humane wildlife removal, exclusion, and damage repair solutions nationwide. We help customers resolve wildlife-related concerns in safe, effective, and environmentally responsible ways while protecting homes, businesses, and communities.

This role is ideal for individuals with a background in construction, repair, or related trades who are committed to craftsmanship and accountability. You’ll play a critical role in preventing future wildlife intrusions by performing exclusion work, repairs, and remediation while maintaining high safety and quality standards.

Critter Control is a brand that invests in its people. If you are a driven professional who embraces our values and upholds our standards of excellence, you’ll find opportunities to succeed, grow, and advance within our organization.

Responsibilities

As a Wildlife Exclusion/Repair Service Technician
at Critter Control, you perform hands-on exclusion, repair, and remediation services for residential and commercial properties. You identify entry points, complete structural repairs, and implement humane wildlife prevention solutions while following safety, technical, and quality guidelines.

What Does a Day in the Life Look Like?

Perform interior and exterior property inspections, including roofs, attics, crawlspaces, and other confined spaces, to identify wildlife entry points and potential vulnerabilities.
Install preventative exclusion materials such as screens, chimney caps, vent covers, and other barriers to prevent wildlife access.
Complete minor repairs to roofs, siding, foundations, and other structural areas where wildlife may gain entry.
Safely remove wildlife using humane trapping and relocation techniques in accordance with company standards and regulations.
Maintain accurate documentation of services performed, materials used, and customer interactions.
Provide clear, detailed reports and review completed scopes of work with customers.
Collaborate with sales and customer service teams to ensure a seamless and positive customer experience.
Follow up with customers to confirm satisfaction and address any additional concerns or recommendations.

What type of benefits will you receive?

Competitive hourly rate + production commission (Hourly Range: $17 - $19)
Estimated Hourly + Commission: $20-$25 an hour - Estimated annual earnings: $45,000 - $60,000.
Comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, and vision insurance.
401k with generous match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP).
6 Paid Holidays Annually!
PTO accrual based on tenure - 3 weeks beginning first full year!
Tuition reimbursement up to $5,250/year (federal max!) OR free tuition on approved programs through Purdue Global!!!
Ongoing training and professional development opportunities!
Supportive team environment with a focus on work-life balance.
Opportunities for career advancement within the Rollins Family of Brands!

Qualifications

What do you need to be successful?

High school diploma or equivalent; college degree is a plus
Valid driver’s license
Proven experience in construction, carpentry, roofing, or other related fields
Ability to work in the field independently
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
Proficiency in using several types of software and applications

What does the work environment look like?

We go where the wildlife goes! Candidates must be physically capable of safely performing the following job duties with or without reasonable accommodation.

Must be able to drive to various locations, often covering large territories.
Frequent walking, standing, and moving through diverse types of terrain, including uneven ground, stairs, roofs, and sometimes slippery or muddy areas.
Ability to work outdoors in various weather conditions (extreme heat, extreme cold, rain, snow, etc.).
Must have the ability to climb stairs and ladders safely.
Must be able to crouch, kneel, bend, and stretch frequently.
Capability to carry and use equipment necessary for inspections and minor control measures (Traps, ladders, inspection tools, etc).
Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds regularly.
Clear verbal communication skills to interact effectively with clients and team members.

Join us in making a positive impact on nuisance wildlife management and become a part of our dedicated team today!

new_jobs.title: Natural Resources Operations Manager
new_jobs.description:
Position Description

Tacoma Power is seeking a Natural Resources Operations Manager to set the direction and drive the delivery of work spanning Northwest fisheries, environmental commitments, and natural resources operations. This leader will establish how scientific, regulatory, and operational priorities are balanced and translate that direction into clear decisions, coordinated work plans, and defined accountability, guiding complex Natural Resources initiatives from concept through implementation and sustained operation.

Northwest fisheries expertise is foundational to this role, and the successful candidate must have professional experience in at least one of the following areas: fisheries resource management, hatchery operations, or fish passage at Northwest hydroelectric facilities. Candidates must also have experience leading major environmental capital projects from initial planning through implementation and transition into sustained, full-scale operation.

Reporting to the Assistant Section Manager for Natural Resources, the Operations Manager directs fisheries resource programs and fish facility operations, working through facility managers, oversees field technician deployment (support for Science and Research, Wildlife and Lands, Water Resources, and Fisheries Operations), and data analytics throughout the department. At the heart of the role is the ability to integrate forward looking strategy, fisheries science, monitoring data, technical information, current FERC license requirements, and operational realities so fish facilities, natural systems, and hydroelectric operations are planned and managed in coordination. This approach supports safe operations, regulatory compliance, long-term stewardship, and reliable, flexible clean power. A defining requirement of this role is the ability to build the structure and capacity needed to take complex Natural Resources initiatives and capital solutions from initial concept through successful implementation and sustained operation. This means setting priorities, aligning resources, and establishing the roles, workflows, and accountability necessary to advance relicensing, current license implementation, and recovery efforts while meeting ongoing operational commitments. The Operations Manager will also guide supervisors and staff through future operational and organizational changes while maintaining continuity. With future studies, relicensing, and evolving regulatory obligations ahead, this leader will be an integral part of the leadership team to position Natural Resources to meet new demands while maintaining safe, reliable operations.

Key Responsibilities

Operational Leadership and Delivery

Lead environmental capital projects from initial planning through successful implementation and transition into sustained operation.
Provide direction and oversight for fisheries resource management and fish facility operations at the Cowlitz and Cushman projects, working with facility managers to ensure alignment and accountability across programs.
Lead department-wide data and analytics, ensuring information is effectively collected, analyzed, and used for reporting and decision support.
Establish field support with integrated priorities and implementation plans across support for Science and Research, Wildlife and Lands, Water Resources, and Fisheries Operations based on operational capacity, safety requirements, regulatory commitments, and long-term objectives

People and Supervisor Leadership

Lead supervisors and multidisciplinary staff across facility operations, field services, technical services, data and analytics, and program delivery.
Support hiring, performance management, coaching, and professional development.
Maintain a regular field presence to understand operational conditions and support staff.

Coordination and Representation

Partner with Natural Resources leadership, Generation, Tribes, agencies, and other stakeholders to align scientific, regulatory, and operational priorities.
Represent operational impacts, resource needs, project dependencies, and opportunity costs in planning, studies, relicensing, and decision-making.

Budget, Contracts, and Resources

Oversee significant operational budgets and sponsor high-profile capital and non-capital projects.
Manage consultant and vendor contracts supporting fish facilities, Natural Resources initiatives, and field operations. Perform owner’s representative functions for assigned capital projects.

Compliance and Accountability

Ensure fish facility operations, fisheries resource management, and related aquatic and terrestrial activities comply with FERC license requirements, applicable permits, and other regulatory obligations.
Maintain effective systems for tracking regulatory commitments, project progress, operational data, documentation, and reporting.
Provide clear operational updates to leadership and elevate significant issues with recommended actions.

Preferred Leadership Attributes

Experience leading operational teams in a regulated fisheries or natural resources environment.
Ability to provide leadership across aquatic and terrestrial resource areas, including disciplines beyond the individual’s primary area of expertise.
A track record of guiding teams through operational or organizational change without disrupting critical services. A collaborative approach to building alignment across scientific, technical, regulatory, and operational disciplines.
Sound judgment when balancing immediate operational needs, ecosystem objectives, regulatory requirements, and clean-power priorities.

Qualifications

Minimum Education*

Bachelor's degree in public or business administration or directly related field

Minimum Experience*

6 years of progressively responsible analytical and/or program coordination or management work in operational, utility, or natural resources environments including 1 year prior at senior, lead or supervisory level

Equivalency: 1 year of experience = 1 year of education

Knowledge & Skills

The successful candidate will demonstrate the following knowledge and skills:

Applied knowledge of fisheries programs, hatchery operations, or fish passage.
Knowledge of the regulatory requirements affecting hydroelectric fisheries programs, including FERC license requirements, permits, and associated compliance obligations.
Experience translating scientific, regulatory, and operational requirements into clear work plans, priorities, and deliverables.
Strong project leadership across interdependent teams, competing priorities, and organizational change.
An understanding of how fish facility operations, field technician deployment, data collection, analysis, and regulatory reporting work together.
Experience managing operational budgets, contracts, and resources in support of program and project commitments.
Effective collaboration with Tribes, agencies, technical experts, utility partners, and other stakeholders.
Sound judgment in identifying operational risks, explaining their impacts, and recommending practical solutions.

Selection Process & Supplemental Information

This recruitment is being managed by Kye Merritt, if you would like to be notified of similar opportunities or stay connected with things going on at Tacoma Public Utilities and the City of Tacoma, connect with me on LinkedIn!

Compensation & Benefits

Pay Details:

Hourly Rate: $67.84 - $95.51

Annual Salary: $141,107.20- $198,660.80

Employee Benefits | City of Tacoma

About Tacoma Power And Natural Resources

Tacoma Power is a municipally owned public power utility that delivers nearly all of its energy from hydroelectric resources. Serving approximately 180,000 customers, we operate in a highly regulated environment where operational reliability, stewardship, and long-term planning are essential.

As one of three operating divisions of Tacoma Public Utilities, alongside Tacoma Water and Tacoma Rail, Tacoma Power offers leaders the opportunity to do meaningful, highly visible work that directly impacts communities, infrastructure, and natural resources.

Our Natural Resources team brings scientific, technical, and operational expertise to meeting the regulatory requirements and stewardship commitments associated with Tacoma Power’s hydroelectric projects. It is a team with a lot of heart and a deep commitment to stewardship. This role is an opportunity to lead people who care deeply about their work and take pride in delivering it well.

HDR is seeking a highly motivated Senior Environmental Planning Project Manager to expand CEQA & NEPA services in the Southern California area. This position is responsible for collaborating and providing technical expertise across HDR’s business groups (Transportation, Resources, Water, BES, Architecture, and Federal). This individual will work with senior management across HDR’s business groups to develop new opportunities, manage and deliver projects, develop staff, and respond to client needs. This is a seller/doer position and requires an individual with a strong character of self-motivation, technical capability, and team leadership.

Responsibilities also include development and review of technical work products (environmental documents and technical studies) and project management. Technical work product includes, but is not limited to the management, preparation, planning, development, and/or analysis/review of technical studies and documentation that meet requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), federal and state permit applications. Work will be accomplished independently and through coordinating or supervising small to large technical and professional teams from local and regional offices. Project Management will include establishing the sequencing of environmental tasks/projects, from financial management of the project through successful completion (managing scope, schedule and budget) of the project using HDR’s technology, standards, and project delivery practices. Candidate will be responsible for task management, staff management, and mentor junior and mid-level environmental planning staff.

In the role of Senior Environmental Planning Project Manager, we'll count on you to:

Direct and coordinate work of single or multidiscipline teams throughout the project's lifecycle (from development & initiation to close-out)
Responsible for any project assignment regardless of size, visibility, number of disciplines, technical complexity or number of staff.
Produce and coordinate several projects concurrently
Establish client relations and be involved with marketing, contractual, design and production meetings
Conduct work sessions for deliverable development in conjunction with other staff and stakeholders
Coordinate staffing and workload through entire project life cycle, and ensure completion of deliverables on schedule
Track financial aspects of projects, and coordinate and adjust work effort with team to ensure that work is completed within parameters of agreed-to budget and schedule
Work with the Accounting, Operational and Business leadership for periodic project reviews
Implement QA/QC procedures
Supervise large project staffs and act as mentor for less-experienced Project Managers
Perform other duties as needed

new_jobs.title: Sr. Regional Enviro Engineer - Water Compliance, AWS Environmental Team
new_jobs.description:
Description

As a Regional Environmental Engineer (REE) specializing in water compliance, you will support water-related environmental compliance at AWS data centers. You will provide technical expertise in permitting and compliance across National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES), Significant Industrial User (SIU) discharge, potable water systems, groundwater wells, onsite wastewater treatment systems, stormwater, and water-quality monitoring and reporting. You will evaluate existing and proposed infrastructure, develop scalable compliance programs and technical standards, monitor environmental performance, and partner with design, construction, operations, and other stakeholders to incorporate water-related regulatory requirements into site design and operation.

Key job responsibilities

Lead water compliance programs for water supply and discharge across US data center locations
Develop and maintain the water compliance program that guides how sites and REEs obtain, renew, modify, interpret, and implement NPDES and other water discharge permits under the Clean Water Act, 40 CFR Part 122, and applicable state regulations, and translate effluent limitations, monitoring, operating, reporting, and notification requirements into site-level compliance programs
Provide guidance on evaluating regulatory applicability and permitting requirements for new sites, expansions, operational changes, and new or modified discharges
Provide guidance on evaluating industrial wastewater and stormwater permitting and compliance, including federal pretreatment under 40 CFR Part 403, local sewer-use ordinances, POTW requirements, pollution-prevention plans, inspections, best management practices, monitoring, and reporting
Provide technical guidance on potable water systems and onsite wastewater systems, including design, operation, monitoring, and compliance under applicable drinking-water and septic requirements

new_jobs.description:
Description

Join a diverse, dynamic, and enthusiastic team of environmental professionals who play a leading role in environmental permitting and compliance at Amazon Web Services (AWS), where we have a history of leading the world in innovative technologies and services. The work of our Regional Environmental Engineers is critical to enabling AWS's growth in the US and around the world.

The AWS Environmental team is an expanding and dynamic team that is critical to enabling AWS’s growth around the world, as well as ensuring compliance of AWS’s global operations, including physical data centers, as well as other AWS facilities, customer-facing enterprises and products. The team has responsibility for architecting and implementing AWS’s global environmental programs. This includes defining and implementing risk management and compliance systems and driving their continuous improvement; setting and refining global policies and procedures; overseeing the development of standards, tools, auditing and metrics, and employee training; ensuring effective engagement by environmental teams on global initiatives, including those that are part of Amazon’s ambitious sustainability goals; providing specialist expertise; and engaging with all AWS business units to provide scalable and effective compliance strategies that support current and future business objectives while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.

You will partner with AWS stakeholders to develop regional and site-specific development strategies enabling the construction and operation of AWS datacenters and infrastructure. You will lead environmental due diligence for site selection and acquisition, develop and execute regional and site-specific environmental permitting strategies, support environmental compliance during design and construction, and prepare for data center operations. This role requires regular engagement throughout the development lifecycle with multiple AWS stakeholders including Real Estate, Legal, Risk, Water, Design, Public Policy, Construction, and Operational teams, as well as external stakeholders including regulatory agencies, consultants, and contractors.

A successful candidate in this role will have a proven track record of delivering multiple, high-priority projects with tight timelines that require strong communication with partner teams, outside consultants and counsel, and regulatory agencies. The candidate must have a strong understanding of multi-media United States environmental permitting, remediation, and compliance requirements associated with large-scale infrastructure including experience with Clean Water Act (CWA) 404 and NPDES permitting. Preference in experience with OH EPA, IDEM, MO EDQ.

Key job responsibilities

Assess environmental risks and requirements and develop mitigations and strategies to support data center siting and development strategies and site-specific project delivery.
Lead technical aspects of environmental due diligence, including Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments, regulatory and permitting evaluations, natural, biological and cultural resource evaluations, and noise assessments.
Deliver environmental permits, approvals, and plans to enable on-time and compliant construction and operations for new data center locations and expansion of existing sites.
Communicate environmental requirements, risks, and activities to internal and external project partners.
Coordinate with partner teams including Real Estate, Design, Water, Legal, Risk, Power, and others to optimize site designs to consider natural resource or operational constraints.
Develop site development and permitting strategies that are environmentally responsible and sustainable while meeting project timelines.
Lead regulatory agency interactions and negotiations in support of environmental permit acquisition and regional development strategies.
Develop, manage and track metrics to evaluate project success

About The Team

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

About AWS

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

new_jobs.description:
Position Title

Florida Conservation Program Manager

Department/Program

Florida Conservation

Reports To

Senior Director of Florida Conservation

Status

Full Time

LOCATION:

Hybrid -
St. Petersburg, Florida (Jacksonville, Miami, and other Florida locations may be considered)

About Ocean Conservancy

For more than 50 years, Ocean Conservancy has delivered effective, evidence-based solutions for the ocean and all who depend on it. Today, we continue to unite science, people and policy to protect our ocean from the greatest challenges it faces: climate change, plastic pollution and biodiversity loss. We are a 501(C)3 headquartered in Washington, D.C. that inspires a worldwide network of partners, advocates and supporters through our comprehensive and clear-eyed approach to ocean conservation. Together, we are securing a healthy ocean and a thriving planet, forever and for everyone.

Position Summary

As a core member of Ocean Conservancy’s Florida Conservation Team, the Florida Conservation Program Manager
will provide critical mission support and added capacity, and will expand and enhance the organization’s ability to work with partners in state and local governments and within the conservation community across Florida. The Manager will serve as a key point of contact with both existing and new local government partners, and will provide lead flagship projects such as grassroots marine debris efforts, marine plastics assessments and grassroots advocacy, sea level rise and climate change initiatives, water quality and abundance interventions, and marine wildlife and habitat protection efforts. The Manager will also represent Ocean Conservancy in public appearances, testimony, and in outreach and education activities.

The Manager will report to the Senior Director of Florida Conservation, and will preferably be based in St. Petersburg, Florida.

Primary Responsibilities

Seek, manage, and expand upon community led initiatives to reduce marine debris and nutrient pollution across Florida, including in key regions that align with the Florida Program Multi Year Strategy – Tampa Bay, Indian River Lagoon, and Biscayne Bay, among others.
Lead strategic development of marine debris positions for the organization that can be deployed at the local government and state levels.
Develop and advance community driven interventions on water quality and marine debris
Participate in the development of grant applications and budget development to attract funding for water quality and marine debris projects in Florida.
Network and partner with state and local government officials on marine conservation priorities in target regions of Florida including South Florida, West Central Florida, Southwest Florida, the I-4 corridor, and Northeast Florida.
Lead the coordination and networking of environmental NGO peers and partners statewide to maximize impact for marine conservation, including in formal Ocean Conservancy led coalitions
Network with impacted stakeholders on issues including water quality and abundance, sea level rise and climate change, marine debris and ocean plastics, and habitat and wildlife
Represent Ocean Conservancy in public settings, including events such as conventions, symposia, and restoration and cleanup events
Provide public testimony to local and state government on marine conservation issues, for example in support of marine debris regulation or fertilizer ordinances
Help develop and refine Ocean Conservancy’s policy positions on marine conservation issues affecting the state

Required Skills/Qualifications/Experience

The successful candidate will, at a minimum, possess the following qualifications:

3-5 years experience in the field of environmental conservation in Florida; an advanced degree (in science, law, policy, or a field related to conservation) will be considered in lieu of experience.
A genuine, ardent passion for the conservation of Florida’s marine environment, and a deep connection to the state and its ecosystems.
Familiarity and experience with the latest marine conservation issues in Florida, and with the potential spectrum of solutions to address those issues – this includes water quality and abundance, nutrient pollution, plastic pollution and marine debris, sea level rise and climate change, and threats to wildlife and habitat, among others.
Innate empathy and a willingness to work with people from across economic and political spectrums and from diverse communities to achieve a greater good
Excellent communications skills, both written and verbal; facility with public speaking; experience and comfort with speaking to the media a plus.
Experience and familiarity with environmental policy analysis and advocacy and a desire to develop policy positions that will have a positive impact for Florida’s marine environment
Highly detail oriented, adaptable, well-organized, and self-starting – ability to work independently and manage up
Highly collaborative and outgoing with large, multi-disciplinary teams

EDUCATION/TRAINING

Bachelor’s degree in a field relevant to Ocean Conservancy’s marine conservation mission

Compensation

Ocean Conservancy is committed to fair pay practices and posts expected salary ranges for each of its positions. Compensation will be commensurate with the candidate’s specialty skills, years of experience, location, and unique background. The expected starting salary range for this role is $70,000 - $80,000 annually. We would welcome the opportunity to connect with potential candidates whose salary requirements may be outside of the expected range.

TO APPLY

If you think you’d be a great fit for the job and are interested in joining Ocean Conservancy’s team, please apply here. Please include a resume and cover letter in one file on your application.

HYBRID WORK ENVIRONMENT

Ocean Conservancy embraces a hybrid work environment, which allows our staff the flexibility to work virtually and in-person while building strong connections across the institution.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Ocean Conservancy provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

We encourage applicants who have a diverse level and range of relevant skills and experiences to apply. A 100% match is not required. We want to support employees’ career growth and in return, our employees help Ocean Conservancy grow into a stronger, more inclusive institution.

Veolia has acquired Clean Earth. As Clean Earth completes its integration into Veolia, recruiting and hiring for this role is being managed in partnership with the Clean Earth talent acquisition team.

Veolia in North America is the top-ranked environmental company in the United States for three consecutive years, and the country’s largest private water operator and technology provider as well as hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It offers a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. Veolia helps commercial, industrial, healthcare, higher education and municipality customers throughout North America. Headquartered in Boston, Veolia has more than 10,000 employees working at more than 350 locations across North America.

Environmental Technician II will be responsible for knowing the location and treatment for inbound waste streams. Environmental Technician II will be able to treat and process waste with onsite equipment. This includes pit mixing, drum pumping, drum dumping, and basic hi-lo and wheel loader skills. Technician must be able to complete required paperwork in accordance with our practices and procedures.

Primary Responsibilities

Complete required paperwork in accordance with our practices and procedures
Collecting samples of inbound waste for compatibility
Unload bulk liquid trucks to proper tank
Resolve and report issues with inbound loads
Operate hi-lo and end loaders in a safe manner
Have knowledge of our waste streams and their treatment protocol.
Performs other reasonably related duties as assigned by management.

Qualifications

Basic requirements:

High School Diploma preferred
2+ years of prior experience working with hazardous materials
Ability to operate equipment, including a forklift and pallet jack
Ability to wear company provided personal protection equipment including eye protection, steel toed shoes, hard hat, gloves, Tyvek coveralls, and respirator
Have the ability to read, write and speak in English
Must be 18 years of age or older

new_jobs.title: Environmental, Health & Safety Officer
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Objective of job

▪Responsible of implementation and maintaining of Environmental, Occupational Health and Safety relevant topics.

▪To comply with Environmental, Occupational Health and Safety legal and DRX standard

Principle activities

▪Advise management in all Occupational Health and Safety relevant topics (e.g. planning, implementing, checking and action) to comply with the law and develop it for ongoing efficiency.

▪Observe the implementation of industrial safety, occupational health, fire protection and accident prevention (e.g. walk through the work areas and report the inadequacies , as well as suggest actions for their elimination; inspect work accidents; train safety personnel; cooperate in approval of hazardous materials and creating instruction for their use, etc.).

▪Laise and coordinate of Fire Fighting System and work with contractors and S.I Dept on inspections , rectifications and trainings.

▪To update the Occupational Health and Safety, and Environment legal based on monthly, and evaluation to ensure all of legal requirement has implemented as required.

▪To analyze the work to indicate possible dangers, including setting and presenting preventive measures and procedures for working safety to employer.

▪To assess the risk in the area of occupational safety (e.g. new processes, products, and new activities).

▪To inspect and assess the operation of the workplace to comply with the work plan and project, or occupational safety measures.

▪To give advice and train the employees to work safely and without any risk of dangers.

▪To examine and appraise the working conditions.

▪To analyze and investigate the causes of accidents, disturbances or illness resulting from working of the employees, and make a report of the investigation, together with suggesting resolution, promptly to the employer.

▪To compile statistical data, analyze, make a report and to give recommendations on accident, illness or disturbance caused by working of the employees.

▪Plan, organize and conduct trainings on first aid, occupational health, environmental.

▪Perform emergency medical care in case of illnesses or accidents on the premises. Creating, updating and maintaining the EHS emergency plan (e.g. fire, medical, etc.)

▪To control Hazardous Material (e.g. registration, updating the hazardous material, creating instruction, label for users, training in chemical safety working for employees

▪To control the first aid room (e.g. medical statistics/reports, medical investigation, treatment, care and advice patients, occupational health, health report; accident reports, treatment protocols for patient records, medicines and medical supplies checking and ordering, etc.)

▪To advice on 6S activity (e.g. planning, implementing, checking and action coordinate with all section etc.)

▪To plan the training on Occupational Health and Safety for new employees, creating the reports, certification.

▪Perform risk assessment refer IS045001, Environmental aspect analysis refer IS014001 for all activities in the plant, update for any changes, and control to use in the areas.

▪Support the safety machine release with project team and S.I Dept

▪Coordinate in regarding of the EHS trainings

▪Manage the safety contractors to ensure that the safety regulations are followed. To check and monitoring the contractor works according to work permit instruction. Perform the safety contractor training.

▪To advice using the personal protective equipment (PPE), control stock to ensure that any PPE is available for employees.

▪Planning, Conducting work environment measurement required by law (e.g. lighting, Noise, Air quality, Pollution released to environment, soil and groundwater contamination etc.)

▪Waste coordinator (e.g. Coordinate with waste disposal contractors for waste release, permission and disposal, recording, monitoring, etc.)

▪Preparation of a EHS monthly report, and input data into the EHS KPls and monitoring .

▪Create the Shopping cart to Order EHS

▪Implementation of the global EHS Standards and ADONIS processes at the site.

▪Preparation of a yearly EHS management review.

▪Management of fire protection measures at the sites.

Special authorizations (e.g. powers of attorney, guidelines competence, authorities, information rights, references to legal or standards-relevant authorized representatives, etc.)

▪Green Book Holder

▪Certified Environmental Professional in Sewage Treatment Plant Operation. (CePSTPO) (Preferred)

▪Certified Environmental Professional in Scheduled Waste Management. (CEPSWAM) (Preferred)

Job Requirements

Specialized knowledge/ education:

▪Bachelor degree or any equivalent education

▪ISO14001:45001 well versed

▪Basic Occupational First Aid, CPR & AED.

▪Fire Protection System Implementation & Coordination

▪EHS Implementation & Coordination

▪Contractor Safety Management

▪Waste Management

Work Experience

▪3-5 yrs

Additional Knowledge

▪Green Book Holder

▪CePSTPO

▪CEPSWAM
